missionPremise: _decisions/2026-08-18_smartcity_kit_component_package.md, active, amended the same day before implementation. The SmartCity kit was ~109 CSS classes and ZERO JS components, so design sync could not consume it: the sync converts a compiled component library, not a class vocabulary. The package is a typed wrapper that renders existing kit classes and owns no styling; sc-kit.css remains the single source of truth for the design. The amendment matters: item 1 as first written forbade any --sc- token declaration while item 4 required the canonical block, so the gate was unsatisfiable for the only useful shape. Item 1 now forbids INVENTING a token rather than CARRYING one.
completionPredicate: A stranger can install the built package, import a component for every class in the shipped vocabulary, render a screen that is markup-identical to the shipped product, and cannot express a token, a colour, a radius, a duration, a bare number, or an absence with no basis through its API. All four hold and each is enforced by a test that has been watched failing.
scopeBasis: Coverage is the WHOLE shipped vocabulary by operator ruling. 'Shipped vocabulary' is defined as the class set extracted from smartcity-dashboards@main web/sc-kit.css + web/shell.css, NOT from 30b section 3.9, which lists the spec reference build's classes. Reason: gate item 3 says an emitted class must exist in sc-kit.css or the product stylesheet, so the stylesheet set is the only set the gate can check, and a component emitting a 30b-only class would render unstyled for every consumer.

coverage.countingRule: distinct class-selector tokens appearing anywhere in vendor/sc-kit.css + vendor/shell.css with CSS comments stripped first. Includes state modifiers (on, open, demo, ok, partial, has-value, word, flush, solo, compact, is-max, is-presented, doc), element-scoped children (t, sub, k, v, n, nm, rail, gl, badge, st-k, sep, id, subj, fill, grow) and the two theme classes. Pseudo-classes, attribute selectors and element selectors are not classes and are not counted.
coverage.howMeasured: By RENDERING, never declared. test/gate3-classes.test.mjs renders every gallery entry plus the composed screen through react-dom/server, parses class attributes out of the HTML, and checks each token against the stylesheet set. A companion test asserts every export of the package index appears in the gallery, so a component cannot dodge the check by being unregistered, and a third asserts each entry's declared `covers` list equals what it actually renders.
coverage.runtimeClasses: Separately, test/runtime-classes.test.mjs extracts the 18 classes app.js assigns at RUNTIME (demo has-value is-max is-presented nm on open p-crit p-info p-ok p-quiet p-warn pill prov rail srcreg t-data word), because index.html alone is not the whole vocabulary in use. All 18 are covered.

componentInventory.note: The planner estimated 18 to 22 components. The real number is 73, roughly 3x. Reason: classes such as t, sub, k, v, n, nm, rail, gl, badge, st-k, sep, id, subj are element-scoped children of a parent class, and covering them 1:1 without inventing wrapper markup makes each a real component or a typed slot. Reported as measured rather than compressed to fit the band.

componentInventory.readingNote: A class appears under every component whose EXAMPLE renders it, so composite examples (ShellTop, CompassSheet, the Data* family) list the classes of the parts they compose. That is the measured output of the example, not a claim of ownership; the owning component for each class is the one whose name is closest to it in this list.

deliberatelyExcluded.what: Every product class named in 30b section 3.9 that does not exist in the shipped stylesheets: sc, avatar, lensswitch, chip, filterbar, toast, ph, btn-danger, btn-icon, field, hint, kbd, seg, cite, cite.model, atomchip, basisline, meter, mx, mxgroup, mxrow, mx-pass, mx-fail, mx-unc, mx-unchecked, finding, gridlines, parcel, sheet, cp-card and its parts, cp-claim, cp-kv, cp-honest, cp-pop, cp-composer, cp-u, cp-a, p4bar, cz-top, cz-nav, cz-body, cz-card, phone.
deliberatelyExcluded.why: They live in the 30b reference build, not in smartcity-dashboards. A component emitting one would fail gate 3 by construction and would render unstyled for any consumer, because the class exists in no stylesheet the consumer loads.
deliberatelyExcluded.consequence: The kit ships NO code-citation component, NO atom chip and NO applicability matrix. Three of the five components 30b calls load-bearing therefore have no wrapper, because the product has not shipped their CSS. This is a real gap in the kit's usefulness for Plan Review surfaces and is the single most important thing in this close for the planner to decide about: either those classes get added to the product stylesheet and then wrapped, or the design agent will invent them.

deliberatelyExcluded.what: The class `roster-lens`, which index.html emits on five sections.
deliberatelyExcluded.why: It appears in neither stylesheet, so emitting it would fail gate 3. The markup-parity instrument normalizes it out of the reference and declares that it does so.
The card forbids it. package.json is publish-ready (name, exports, files, types) and `npm pack` is exercised by the consumer test, but nothing was published.

deliberatelyExcluded.what: No component rewrite of any shipped surface.
deliberatelyExcluded.why: The ruling's scope section: Dashboards, Plan Review and Smart Files keep their current markup until a card says otherwise. smartcity-dashboards was cloned read-only and not modified.

gates.rule: The package declares no --sc- token of its own. It may carry the canonical token block.
gates.how: 1a: no package-AUTHORED file declares a --sc- token (whole repo except vendor/, dist/, harness/out/, package-lock.json, and one named self-exclusion). 1b: the only token-declaring files are the two registered vendor copies, each matching its pinned LF-normalized sha256. 1c: the carried block differs from the 30b section 4.1 extract by EXACTLY one pre-registered declaration line. 1d: the build did not modify the token file on its way into dist.
gates.watchedFailing: yes, three ways: a component file declaring its own token; the carried token file edited; a token invented inside the carried block. All three FIRED and named the violation.
gates.exclusionSet: exactly one file, test/gate1-tokens.test.mjs, which must quote the pinned token line in order to pin it. scripts/prove-gates.mjs was NOT excluded; its payloads are assembled at runtime instead, so the exclusion set stays at one.

gates.rule: No component file contains a hex colour, an rgb() value, or a hardcoded px radius or duration.
gates.how: Regex scan of every file under src/ for hex colours, rgb/rgba, px lengths, ms and s durations. The scan is over RAW BYTES including comments, and the exclusion set is empty. Deliberate: a comment-stripping exclusion needs a stripper, and a stripper is one template literal away from being wrong. The cost is that a comment may not spell a value either.
gates.watchedFailing: yes, twice: a component declaring a hex colour, and a component declaring a px radius. Both FIRED and named the rule and the line.

gates.rule: Every class a component emits exists in sc-kit.css or the product stylesheet.
gates.how: STRUCTURAL. Every export is rendered through examples/gallery.tsx in every variant, class attributes are parsed out of the rendered HTML, and each token is checked against the 109-class stylesheet set. Nothing reads a hand-written class list. Three supporting assertions close the loopholes: every export must appear in the gallery; every gallery entry must name a real export; and each entry's declared coverage must equal what it renders.
gates.watchedFailing: yes, twice: a component emitting a class no stylesheet defines, and a new export left unregistered in the gallery. Both FIRED and named the class or the export.

gates.rule: The package adds no CSS rule of its own.
gates.how: Every .css file anywhere in the repo must be a registered copy in vendor/UPSTREAM.json and match its pin, or a byte copy of one produced by the build. An authored stylesheet fails by EXISTING, so there is no directory to hide one in. Plus a scan of src/ for styling escape hatches (style element, styled-components, css tagged template, inline style prop, stylesheet import, insertRule) and a type-level assertion that className and style are removed from the shared prop bag.
gates.watchedFailing: yes, twice: the package authoring a stylesheet, and a component importing one. Both FIRED and named the file or the hatch.

negativeSuite.method: Injects one real violation per gate into a temporary COPY of the repo (never the working tree), runs that gate, and requires the gate to FAIL and to NAME the violation in its message. A gate that fails for an unrelated reason does not score.
negativeSuite.result: 16 of 16 injected violations caught and named
negativeSuite.beyondTheFourGates: law 3 quiet default flipped; Panel gaining an elevation prop; a component adding a wrapper the product does not have; upstream drifting from the copy; a forbidden string reaching a file; the product assigning a class no stylesheet defines; the kit ceasing to cover a runtime class.
negativeSuite.firstRunScored: 13 of 15. Two cases failed the test but did not name the violation, which meant my expected-message strings were wrong, not the gates. Recorded because a negative suite tuned until it reads clean is worth nothing.

typeLevelGates.how: test/consumer.test.mjs compiles 10 programs that violate the design law against the EMITTED declarations in an installed tarball, and requires the compiler to reject each ON THE OFFENDING LINE. A rejection caused by an unrelated error does not count.
shapesRejected: a Metric with no counting rule
a Metric that is both a value and an unknown
a type step outside the ramp
a Pill with an emphasis lever
a provenance chip with no source
an environment badge with no environment
typeLevelGates.caughtDuringDevelopment: These 10 first 'passed' while @types/react was unresolvable, so tsc was failing on every file including the good one. The good-file typecheck failing is what exposed it. The line-citation requirement was added as a result.

renderedComparisons.automated: 17 element-level comparisons against vendor/index.html (a pinned copy of the shipped page) plus three composed comparisons: the whole top bar, the whole sidebar, and the whole Overview city-manager lens. Comparison is over tag, class, element order, nesting and text; attributes, ids, hidden elements and whitespace are normalized and the normalization contract is stated in test/_markup.mjs where its output is read.
renderedComparisons.result: All 20 identical. The composed Overview lens is markup-identical to section#lens-city-manager as shipped.
renderedComparisons.visual: Headless Chrome screenshots at 1600x1000 of the same lens rendered two ways through the same two stylesheets: harness/out/screen-kit.png (composed from kit components) and harness/out/screen-product.png (the shipped page with its runtime script removed). Read side by side, they are indistinguishable. Four gallery pages and a light-theme pass were also rendered and read.
renderedComparisons.whatTheComparisonFound: Four component defects that were green on types and wrong on markup, each fixed in the component rather than papered over in the composition: MountNote rendered b > span.t-data where the product ships b.t-data; Prov wrapped its detail in a span while the shipped chip is not uniform (5 instances carry bare text after the separator, 1 a span, 1 two spans); Grow was span-only while the top bar ships div.grow; ShellNav declared the open state as covered while no example rendered it. Six gallery entries also declared coverage that did not match what they rendered.
renderedComparisons.honestLimit: The visual half is a human read of two images, not a pixel diff. The automated half is the markup comparison. Stated rather than implied.

findings.claim: smartcity-dashboards web/sc-kit.css is NOT byte-identical to 30b section 4.1, so gate item 1 read strictly against 30b would fail on the very file the card orders copied verbatim.
findings.evidence: LF-normalized. 30b 4.1 = 3794 bytes, sha256 20e08faf61e449e075289cbfdfef146b894538bed3f6e0ef8adba7f16b4614f9. Shipped = 4329 bytes, sha256 2cdd0bf876ee24224eb0e976c4c29f1f79bb37324a53aac50d3d78feec113ef2. With comments stripped the delta is exactly ONE declaration line: --sc-spring-stiffness:320; --sc-spring-damping:32; --sc-spring-mass:0.9. Every token VALUE is identical.
findings.assessment: Not a fork. 30b section 1.7 names --sc-spring as stiffness 320 / damping 32 / mass 0.9; the shipped file expresses that one doc token as three CSS custom properties. Doc-vs-shipped expression drift.
findings.disposition: gate 1c pins this exact delta, so any NEW divergence fails. The reconciliation belongs in the doc or the product, not in the kit.

findings.severity: medium, decided in this card and flagged
findings.claim: Shipping only sc-kit.css would make every component render unstyled, because the component classes live in shell.css.
findings.disposition: The package ships BOTH files as byte copies, each hash-pinned and drift-tested. Neither is authored here. The card named only sc-kit.css explicitly, so this is a decision I made and it is flagged rather than buried.

findings.claim: Three of the five components 30b calls load-bearing have no shipped CSS, so the kit cannot wrap them: the code-citation chip, the atom chip and the applicability matrix.
findings.consequence: A design agent drawing the Plan Review queue and console (30c F1 to F7) will have to invent all three, which is precisely the failure this package exists to prevent. The kit closes the gap for the Dashboards vocabulary and leaves it open for the review surfaces.
findings.disposition: Named for the planner. The fix is a card that adds those classes to the product stylesheet, after which wrapping them is small.

findings.claim: A local run reported the suite green while gate 1a was already failing on scripts/prove-gates.mjs, and CI is what surfaced it.
findings.evidence: A local `npm test` was recorded as 66 tests / 65 pass / 0 fail with scripts/prove-gates.mjs already present carrying a literal --sc- declaration. Re-running the same suite on the same tree afterwards reproduced the failure. I could not reconstruct why the earlier run reported clean and am recording the discrepancy rather than rounding it off.
findings.disposition: CI is authoritative, which is the standing rule and is now demonstrated rather than asserted. Two numbers that should agree and did not.

findings.claim: Checking the upstream repo out INSIDE the workspace made three repo-wide scans report the upstream product as this package's violations.
findings.disposition: Fixed in two independent places on purpose: CI moves the checkout out of the workspace, and test/_lib.mjs walk() refuses to descend into a nested clone and REPORTS what it refused. One rule with one implementation is one CI edit away from being gone.

findings.claim: The repo was created public with no licence. A LICENSE was added stating proprietary terms and granting nothing, naming Legacy Group ATX LLC as the copyright holder.
findings.disposition: The terms are the conservative fill for a public repo with none. The ENTITY NAME is my inference from the portfolio structure and has not been confirmed; smartcity-dashboards carries no LICENSE at all, so there was no precedent to copy. Operator should confirm or correct the holder.

findings.claim: The repository had no commits, so the first push made g82/kit-wrapper the default branch and there was nothing to open a pull request against.
findings.disposition: An empty root commit was pushed as main, the default branch was set to it, and the work branch was joined to it so the PR has a common ancestor. main carries no files from this card. No force-push was used.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: Client-side React. Every render in this suite is renderToStaticMarkup. Nothing hydrates, nothing mounts in a DOM, and no event handler is fired.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: onClick, aria-expanded toggling, and the open/active state props are asserted as CLASS OUTPUT only. A component that emits the right class and mishandles an interaction would pass.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.differsForAConsumer: Yes. A consumer runs these in a browser with react-dom/client. Hydration mismatches, ref behaviour and event wiring are untested here.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: Responsive and theme behaviour. The stylesheet has three media blocks (max-width 1180, max-width 900, prefers-reduced-motion) and a dark-theme block. No test renders at a narrow viewport or in reduced-motion.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: MenuButton renders correctly and is display:none above the breakpoint, so its visible behaviour is only observed in the light and dark gallery screenshots at one width. ShellNav open is asserted as a class, never as a visible sheet.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.differsForAConsumer: Yes, for anyone shipping to a phone.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: The Stage and Compass presentation states. is-presented, is-max, cp-scrim and stage-scrim are position:fixed and are rendered in the gallery inside a transformed container so they do not cover the page.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: Their real geometry, which the product drives with inline transforms from app.js, is not exercised at all. The kit renders the container; the motion is the product's.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.differsForAConsumer: Yes. A consumer wiring a stage must supply the positioning the product supplies.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: Populated .dt rows have no static reference in index.html; the shipped tbody is empty and app.js builds the rows. Parity for the ROW shape was verified against app.js source (td(recordId,'id'), td(subject,'subj'), a span.t-data due cell, a span.pill.p-* status cell) and against the runtime class extractor, not against rendered product markup.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: If app.js changes the row structure without changing a class, the runtime-class test still passes and no parity test notices.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.differsForAConsumer: No, this is an instrument gap on both sides.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: Classes with a stylesheet rule but no shipped usage: sub, fill, compact, ok. They are rendered by the kit and covered by gate 3, but there is no product element to compare them against, so markup parity cannot check them.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: Their markup is my reading of the CSS selector, not a copy of shipped markup.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: The build is exercised only through npm test on Node 22 (CI) and 24 (local). No bundler integration test: no webpack, Vite, Next or esbuild consumer build is run against the package.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: The exports map is proven by Node resolution and by tsc with moduleResolution Bundler. A bundler that reads the map differently is untested.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.differsForAConsumer: YES, and this is the most likely place a consumer hits something the suite did not. In particular the CSS side-effect declaration and the sc-kit.css / shell.css subpaths are resolved by Node require.resolve here, not by a bundler's CSS pipeline.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: npm publish and registry install. The consumer test packs a tarball and extracts it by hand; it never runs `npm install @empressaio/smartcity-kit` from a registry.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: Registry-side concerns (scope access, .npmignore interaction, provenance) are untested.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.differsForAConsumer: Yes, and publishing is out of scope for this card by instruction.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: The Windows path in the consumer test. runNpm uses shell:true only on win32 and the pack destination is quoted only there.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: Each platform exercises one branch and neither exercises both. The Linux branch is covered by CI, the Windows branch by the local run; a change to one is not checked by the other.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.differsForAConsumer: Yes, and this already bit once: the quoting was correct on Windows and wrong on Linux, and only CI caught it.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: The screenshot harness itself has no test. If render-harness.mjs stops producing a page, nothing fails.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: The visual proof is a manual step, run and read by the agent, not a gate.

codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.path: vendor-parity arm B is skipped whenever SC_DASHBOARDS_DIR is unset, which is every local run that does not set it.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.consequence: A local `npm test` cannot see upstream drift. It says so in its own output and CI fails the job if the check skipped, but the local suite is weaker than it looks.
codePathsTestsDoNotExercise.differsForAConsumer: Yes, in the sense that a contributor running tests locally is running a subset.

constraintsHonored: smartcity-dashboards cloned read-only at /p/tmp/b82-dash and NOT modified. plan-review, smart-files and smartcity-os-prod were never opened.
Forbidden strings permitflow, CitizenConnect, leaflet, pipedrive, stripe.com: zero occurrences in any file in the repo, enforced by test/constraints.test.mjs and proven able to fire.
Bastrop and Chestnut: zero occurrences. Neither is asserted as content and neither was needed as a refusal needle in this repo.

No sample city data beyond the fixture pack. Every example record is a verbatim capture of generatePipelineRecords({ cityKey: 'fixture-city', generatesFixtures: true }) from smartcity-dashboards@cdfca39, all 14 carrying origin 'fixture' and fixture true, asserted by test. The only parcel identifier anywhere is 48021:34137, the one demo fixture the product itself labels as one, asserted by test.

Every verification command exit-bounded. No server was started; the screenshot harness renders file:// URLs and every Chrome invocation is a one-shot --screenshot with a timeout. Nothing was left running.
No sub-agents spawned. Verification was not delegated.

docRepoEdits.note: doc_repo commits are planner-owned. These three files are written and left uncommitted.

whatRemainsOpen: PR #1 is open and mergeable with CI conclusion 'success'. Merge is the planner's.
F-3: the code-citation chip, the atom chip and the applicability matrix have no shipped CSS and therefore no wrapper. This is the gap that will bite the Plan Review surfaces first.
F-1: 30b section 4.1 and web/sc-kit.css disagree by one declaration line. Reconcile in one direction; the kit pins the current gap.
F-6: the LICENSE copyright holder needs operator confirmation.

Design sync itself is explicitly not in this card and has not been attempted or verified. The ruling's own reversal criterion is that the package has no justification if design sync turns out not to consume it, and nothing here tests that it does.
No bundler integration test. Named above as the most likely consumer-side surprise.
The package is version 0.1.0 and unpublished.
